dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent, and I'll be evaluating your symptoms today. Could you describe exactly where you feel the pain and whether it began suddenly or over time?

It's a burning pain that starts in my neck and travels all the way down my arms. It's been bothering me for about a year now, but the weakness in my hands has really gotten worse over the last three months.

Have you noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning your shirt or any changes in your balance while walking? This information helps me determine if the spinal cord itself is involved.

Actually, I have been struggling with my shirts lately because my hands feel so weak, and I've noticed my muscles twitching a bit. My fingers also feel like they're tingling or "asleep" most of the time. As far as walking goes, I haven't noticed much change in my balance, but the pain in my neck is constant.

Have you experienced any changes in your bladder or bowel control since these symptoms began? I would also like to know if you've had any recent injuries to your neck or spine. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine
RESULTS: MRI_Spine: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

Have you noticed any difficulty sensing hot or cold temperatures in your hands, even if you can still feel someone touching them? I'm going to order a brain scan to look for any related structural issues. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

That is very helpful to know. Have you noticed if you have trouble feeling hot or cold temperatures in your hands, such as when washing dishes or holding a hot mug? Also, did you ever have any significant neck injuries in the past?

Now that you mention it, I have burnt my fingers on a hot stove a few times without even realizing it until I saw the blister. As for injuries, I was in a pretty bad car accident about three years ago that really jolted my neck.

Based on the presence of the syrinx on your MRI and your loss of temperature sensation, it appears your symptoms are linked to a specific condition. To be certain, have you noticed any visible thinning or

Yes, I have noticed that the muscles in my hands look a bit thinner and more wasted than they used to. It's especially clear between my thumb and index finger. Along with that, I keep seeing those little twitches under my skin.

Given the wasting in your hands and your history of neck trauma, I would like to check your reflexes and sensory levels. Have you noticed any unusual curvature in your spine or persistent headaches, particularly when
I haven't noticed my spine looking crooked, but I do get these sharp headaches sometimes. They usually seem to flare up whenever I have to cough or strain myself.

Those headaches when straining are quite characteristic of the pressure changes caused by the cavity in your spinal cord. Since we've confirmed the syrinx on your MRI and your clinical symptoms match perfectly, I have
I understand. Does this mean the accident from a few years ago is finally catching up with me? I'm just worried about how much weaker my hands might get if we don't do something soon.

It is very likely that the trauma from your accident caused this cavity, or syrinx, to form within your spinal cord. Does the loss of temperature sensation extend across your shoulders and upper back, almost like a cape? This will help me confirm the exact extent of the condition.

That’s exactly right, it feels just like a cape draped over my shoulders and down my back. In those areas, I can't really tell if something is hot or cold anymore. It’s a very strange sensation, or I guess, a lack of one.

The characteristic "cape-like" distribution of sensory loss, combined with the muscle wasting in your hands and the syrinx confirmed on your MRI, confirms the diagnosis. Your history of trauma followed

It's a relief to finally have an explanation, though it's frightening to think there's a cavity inside my spine. What are the next steps to keep this from getting worse or to help me get some strength back in my hands? I just want to be able to use my fingers properly again without burning myself.
We will refer you to a neurosurgeon to discuss surgical options to drain the syrinx and prevent further nerve damage. I am pleased we have a clear path forward for your treatment. DIAGNOSIS READY
